transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

I guess… I came in because I’m just tired all the time. Like, by midmorning at work, after I’ve only been reviewing claim files or walking one of the junior adjusters through something, I already feel like my body and my brain are running on empty.

And I know everybody gets tired—my sister says that all the time, she’s always comparing who’s more exhausted—but this feels like I’m dragging through the day before it’s even really started.
Have you noticed feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy along with the fatigue?

Yeah… I mean, I think so. It’s not like I’m crying all day or anything dramatic, but most days it’s like there’s this gray film over everything.

Like my husband can be perfectly kind, and we’ll be making dinner, or the kids and family are around cooking together—well, not kids, they’re grown, but you know what I mean—and I’m there, I’m doing what I’m supposed to do. I chop vegetables, I answer questions, I smile at the right time. But it doesn’t really land the way it used to. I don’t feel the enjoyment in it, not really. It’s more like I’m watching myself go through the motions.
Have you found that you don’t take pleasure in things you used to enjoy, even activities that were important to you before?

Yes… yeah, I think that’s right. It’s like I still do the things, you know? My husband will be sweet, and we’ll be cooking with the family, and I’m chopping onions or setting things out, and everyone’s talking over each other like usual.

And I should feel… I don’t know, warmed by it, or happy, because I used to. But most days it’s like there’s this gray film over everything. I can smile and keep going through the motions, but the enjoyment doesn’t really get through the way it used to.
Do these feelings of tiredness and going through the motions happen most of the day, nearly every day, or do they come and go throughout the day or week?

It’s… it’s most days, honestly. I came in because I’m tired all the time. Like by midmorning at work, after just reviewing claim files or walking one of the junior adjusters through something, I already feel like my body and my brain are running on empty.

And then I start thinking, well, maybe everyone feels like this at work, because claims can be tedious and there’s always some file missing something, and the newer people need help with the same issues over and over… but this feels heavier than that. It’s not just a bad afternoon here or there.

How long have you been feeling this way — the fatigue, the gray film over everything, and not feeling enjoyment — have these been going on for at least two weeks, or have they lasted longer, like for months or more?

Longer. Definitely longer than two weeks.

I think it started around… a little over three years ago now. Maybe three years and a few months? It was when I got moved into that higher-responsibility role at work, mentoring the other adjusters and helping oversee the new workflow systems. At first I told myself it was just the change, you know, everybody was stressed and the system was a mess, and people were asking me questions all day long.

But it just… never really lifted. So yes, it’s been months and months—really about three years and three months.
Between times when you felt this way, have you had periods where your mood improved and you felt like your usual self for a while?

Not really in any lasting way. I mean, there are moments where I’m distracted or things feel a little lighter, like if I’m busy with something at home or work, but I don’t think I’ve gone back to feeling like my usual self.

It’s been pretty steady since that work change, when I got moved into the role mentoring the other adjusters and dealing with the new workflow systems. That was… about three years and three months ago now, and it just kind of settled in and stayed.
Have there been any periods—even brief ones—when you felt clearly better and had a return of your usual mood and energy, not just moments of distraction or slight improvement?

I don’t think there’s been a clear stretch like that, no. I keep trying to think if there was a week or something where I felt like, “Oh, there I am again,” but it’s more like little blips, not really a return to normal.

This has basically been going on since I was moved into that higher-responsibility role at work—mentoring the adjusters, overseeing those new workflow systems. That was about three years and three months ago. Funny, I remember it because everyone was complaining about the system rollout and the way the files were getting routed, and I kept thinking, once this settles down I’ll feel better… but it just never really did.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight over the course of these three years—like eating more or less than usual, or gaining or losing weight without trying?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I don’t think there’s been some big obvious change where my clothes suddenly didn’t fit or anything like that.

My eating is kind of… ordinary, I guess? Some days I don’t feel like making much, but then I’ll just snack or eat whatever’s easy. I haven’t been tracking it. My sister tracks everything on some app and tells me I should, but I can barely remember to write down mileage for work sometimes, so…

So, no, I haven’t noticed a major weight change without trying. At least not one that stands out to me.
Have you had trouble sleeping—like trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or waking up too early—or have you been sleeping more than usual during this time?

I don’t know that I’ve kept track well enough to say. Sleep is… kind of one of those things I complain about and then forget the details, if that makes sense.

Some nights I’m in bed and I’m thinking about whatever happened that day, or a file I need to handle, and then I’ll look at the clock and get annoyed with myself. But other times I’m just tired and I go to sleep. I couldn’t tell you if it’s more falling asleep or waking up or anything like that.

My neighbor has one of those watches that tells her her “sleep score,” and she’s always talking about deep sleep and REM, and I honestly think if I had that information it would just give me one more thing to worry about. So… I guess I haven’t noticed a clear pattern, not enough to say I’m sleeping a lot more or a lot less.
Have you found yourself feeling guilty or blaming yourself for things more than usual, even when it’s not really your fault?

I’m not sure I’d say guilty, exactly. I mean, I second-guess myself a lot, but with my job you kind of have to, because if you miss something in a claim file it can come back around and then everyone has an opinion about how you handled it.

But blaming myself for things that aren’t my fault… I don’t know. Maybe sometimes I replay conversations and think I should’ve said something differently. Then again, my sister does that too, and she’s always telling me she lies awake thinking about some thing she said in 1998, so maybe that’s just normal.

So… I guess I haven’t noticed it as some big new thing, no. Not more than usual, at least.
Have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual, or that you can't sit still and feel restless?

I don’t think so? I mean, nobody’s told me I’m moving slowly or anything like that. I’m not, like, shuffling around the office or pacing holes in the carpet.

Sometimes at work I get up and wander over to the copier or the break room, but honestly half the time that’s because the printer jams or someone left their lunch in the microwave too long and everyone’s making a big production about it. Our office is kind of like that—little dramas over nothing.

But as far as feeling like I can’t sit still, or being noticeably slowed down… I haven’t really noticed that, no.
Have you ever found yourself thinking about death or dying, or wished you could just not wake up?

I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I mean, I’ve thought about death in the way you do when someone your age starts hearing about people from high school getting sick, or you see something on the news and it sticks with you. My coworker is always sending around those fundraiser links for someone’s cousin, and it kind of makes you think, you know?

But if you mean, like… wishing I wouldn’t wake up, I don’t know. I don’t think I’ve really sat with it like that. It’s not something I’ve been tracking or anything.
Have you lost interest in activities you used to look forward to, like hobbies, work tasks, or time with friends, even things that used to feel meaningful or satisfying?

Yeah… I think so. It’s not that I don’t do things, exactly. I still show up, I still make dinner sometimes, I still sit with my husband or help when the family’s around cooking or whatever. We have this whole thing where everybody gets in the kitchen and somehow uses every pan in the house, and then no one knows who left the cabinet open—sorry, that’s not really the point.

The point is, most days it feels like there’s this gray film over everything. Like I’m there, and people are being kind, and on paper it should feel nice or satisfying, but I’m just kind of going through the motions. I don’t get the same feeling from it that I used to.
